_note: Newly elected state legislative members, stated positions, fourth wave (November 2026): Alaska, Montana, South Dakota, Vermont and Utah. The November 3, 2026 State Senate and State House winners on seats whose district board already exists, whom the roster held as candidate rows with no stance entries, and the issue keys their stated positions were filed on in politician-stances.js (regenerated into politician-stances-ext.js). Every entry is the member-elect's own published position, read from the campaign's own priorities, issues or platform page and marked claim:'campaign'; nothing is inferred from party. Each member has a published race call naming them: a news outlet's call, or the state's own results page with every precinct reported. 'district' is the roster's district as written (Vermont districts are named, Alaska Senate districts lettered); 'boards' are the board files that seat already had. Profiles, roster rows, vote records, the drawer and the related-issues map are unchanged. Earlier waves: db/newly-elected-state-legislative-stated-2026-11.json (Michigan), -wave2.json (Colorado, Nevada, Minnesota), -wave3.json (Tennessee, Maine, Nebraska, Rhode Island, Idaho). Read by scripts/test-newly-elected-state-legislative-stated-2026-wave4.mjs.
boards: Every seat in the set already has a district board (district-<state>-<sd|hd>-<n>[-p<seat>].html); no board was opened for this pass.

members.name: Kathy C. Simpler
members.raceCallNote: Alaska Division of Elections summary (unofficial, 12 of 12 precincts in): Simpler (NON) 2,160 (55.44%), Prout (REP) 1,729 (44.38%). That is an outright first-choice majority, so no RCV runoff, with a 431-vote margin. KMXT (11/4) says she is 'set to win by commanding margins'. ADN (11/4) says she 'led with 55.4%' with all precincts reporting. Open seat: Stutes left it to run for Senate C. This is her first state office.

members.name: Lisa M. Keller
members.raceCallNote: Alaska Division of Elections summary (unofficial, all precincts): Keller (DEM) 3,240 (90.03%) vs write-ins 9.97%. She was the only name on the ballot after Felix Rivera withdrew and a court left Republican Sarah Short off (ADN 9/30/2026). MultiState lists her as the HD-13 winner. Open seat: Rep. Andy Josephson is retiring. Keller was a legislative aide and has never held the seat.

members.name: Margaret Mitchell
members.raceCallNote: Montana Free Press live blog: Mitchell (D) won the open SD 10 seat by 14 points over Jessica Dyrdahl (R). Daily Montanan (dailymontanan.com/2026/11/04/dems-flip-seats-in-montana-legislature/) also reports 3,701-2,832 with all precincts in, a flip of the seat Jeremy Trebas left. MT SOS shows 6/6 precincts fully reported. She is a first-time legislator ('This will be new to me').

members.name: Jim Riley
members.raceCallNote: Montana Secretary of State results page (unofficial, updated 11/4/2026 7:10 PM): HD 6 6/6 precincts fully reported, Riley (R) 3,991 to Darren Fix (D) 2,323 (~63-37). Daily Inter Lake and Flathead Beacon results tables show the same lead. Open seat (Amy Regier ran for SD 4); Flathead Beacon describes Riley as new to politics.

members.name: Michelle Bianco
members.raceCallNote: Montana Secretary of State results page (unofficial, updated 11/4/2026 7:10 PM): HD 1 12/12 precincts fully reported, Bianco (R) 4,476 to Dakota V Adams (D) 1,404 (76-24). Flathead Beacon and Daily Inter Lake tables match. No incumbent ran (Rep. Neil Duram held the seat); Bianco is a first-time candidate.

members.name: Adam Bair
members.raceCallNote: Sioux Falls Argus Leader (Morgan Matzen, via Yahoo), Nov. 4: 'Newcomers Kathleen Brudvig (D) and Adam Bair (D) won' District 10 House; Bair 28% (3,764) vs. Pohlman (R) 21% (2,852), ~900-vote margin for 2nd seat.

members.name: Ali Rae Horsted
members.raceCallNote: Sioux Falls Argus Leader (via Yahoo), Nov. 4: Kolbeck (R) 35% and newcomer Horsted (D) 33% win District 13 House; 'Horsted ousted incumbent John Hughes (R)' (5,588 vs 5,276, ~312 votes; not on the listed possible-recount races).

members.name: June CopperStad
members.raceCallNote: Sioux Falls Argus Leader (via Yahoo), Nov. 4: 'incumbent Kadyn Wittman (D) and newcomer June CopperStad (D)' won District 15 House with 33% and 30%; CopperStad 2,906 vs. Tschetter (R) 1,886.

members.name: Jeff Haylon
members.raceCallNote: VTDigger: AP called Rutland-9 for Democrat Jeff Haylon over Republican Aida Nielsen around 8 p.m., Haylon leading by more than 20 points; open seat vacated by Rep. Todd Nielsen. VTDigger 11/4 follow-up confirms the win.

members.name: Phoebe Tucker
members.raceCallNote: VTDigger: AP called Rutland-Windsor for Democratic newcomer Phoebe Tucker over incumbent Rep. Kevin Winter (R) around 9 p.m., Tucker leading by more than 12 points; VTDigger 11/4 follow-up says Tucker won.

members.name: Kim Gleason
members.raceCallNote: VTDigger reports Democratic challenger Kim Gleason 'pulled off' the first Senate flip, unseating Sen. Pat Brennan (R); Colchester Sun/WCAX results: Gleason 5,836 (53.4%) to Brennan 5,076 (46.4%), ~760-vote margin.

members.name: Hannah Sessions
members.raceCallNote: VTDigger: Sen. Ruth Hardy and newcomer Hannah Sessions (D) won both Addison seats, overcoming Sen. Steve Heffernan (R) and Andrew Klein (R). Unofficial SOS results: Sessions 12,668 (31.8%), Hardy 12,510, Heffernan 7,933 (19.9%), Klein 6,689 — ~4,700-vote margin over 3rd.

members.name: Iva Williams
members.raceCallNote: Deseret News (also on KSL), Nov 4: Rep. Clint Okerlund (R-Sandy) 'trails by nearly 1,600 votes to Democrat Iva Williams and has conceded the race.' UND election-night count: Williams 55.79% to Okerlund 44.21%. She unseated the incumbent, so she is new.
